sections.h2: Where does Cherokee County send the property tax bill, and who sets the value?
sections.html:
Cherokee County splits the work between two offices on the same stretch of Marietta Highway in Canton. The Tax Commissioner bills and collects real estate, personal property, public utility, timber, motor vehicle and mobile home taxes and then disburses them to the state, county, school and city governments. The Tax Assessors' Office decides what your property is worth and which exemptions you receive.

  • Tax Commissioner: 678-493-6400, cherokeecountytax.com. Main office at 2780 Marietta Hwy, Canton, and an annex at 155 Towne Lake Pkwy, Woodstock, both open 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Tax Assessors' Office: 678-493-6120, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton. Returns are filed here between January 1 and April 1.
  • City tax offices bill separately inside Ball Ground, Canton, Holly Springs, Mountain Park, Nelson, Waleska and Woodstock, so check whether your address is incorporated.

Assessors may visit a property after an appeal, a new return, new construction or a conservation use application. Their staff carry county photo identification and drive marked county vehicles, and answering their questions is voluntary.

sections.h2: What is Cherokee County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Cherokee County was created by the General Assembly on December 26, 1831, and Canton became the seat after the early county seat of Etowah was renamed. Growth took off after the first phase of Interstate 575 opened in 1979. The freeway bisects the county from Kennesaw through Woodstock, Holly Springs and Canton to Ball Ground, and the southern end nearest Atlanta is the most densely settled.

The county covers 434 square miles, of which 422 are land. Lake Allatoona fills much of the southwest corner, and the north climbs toward the foothills, with Bear Mountain at 2,297 feet the highest listed summit. Reinhardt University is in Waleska, Chattahoochee Technical College has campuses in Woodstock and Canton, and one school district, the Cherokee County School District, serves every address.

QuickFacts puts the 2025 population at 299,273, a 12.2% rise from the 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a median owner-occupied home value of $435,100, a median household income of $108,115 and 77.3% owner occupancy. Workers average a 31.3 minute commute, and 1,524 building permits were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: When are Cherokee County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in September and are due November 15. Anything unpaid after that date is delinquent, and the Tax Commissioner reminds owners that a tax lien attaches to the property once taxes go delinquent. Mobile home bills go out in January and are due on or before April 1.

The county's 2026 rates, as the Tax Commissioner prints them, are in the table. A mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, and Georgia sets assessed value at 40% of fair market value.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Cherokee County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. Georgia's uniform appeal form lets you pick a Board of Equalization hearing, a hearing officer or arbitration, and an appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

The county appraisal staff values property with sales comparison, cost and income approaches and tests the results statistically by area, neighborhood and class of property. A good appeal answers those methods with your own evidence.

  • Recent closed sales of similar houses nearby, with dates and prices.
  • Photos and repair estimates that show condition problems the record may not reflect.
  • A copy of your settlement statement or warranty deed if you bought the property recently.

A complaint about the amount of tax is not an appeal ground, because the assessors do not set millage rates. Those are set by the governing bodies named on your bill.

sections.h2: How do I claim a homestead exemption in Cherokee County?
sections.html:
Apply in person at the Tax Assessors' Office with a valid Georgia driver's license or ID showing the current address of the property. Bring your settlement statement or warranty deed too, since staff print and complete the application when you arrive.

The state's standard homestead exemption applies to an owner-occupied primary residence, and the county can add to it. Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that an application is generally accepted year-round but must arrive by April 1 to count for that tax year, and that failing to apply waives the exemption. Ask the Assessors' Office which Cherokee County exemptions for seniors, disabled veterans or surviving spouses fit your situation, since the amounts change.

Any exemption is tied to the person who applied. When you sell, the buyer starts fresh with a new application.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell in Cherokee County?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes the owner of record on January 1, and the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner says plainly that the law gives its office no way to prorate tax for part of a year. Any split has to be agreed between buyer and seller at closing.

A buyer who closes in the fall will not automatically get a bill. The Tax Commissioner asks that the closing settlement statement be sent to the office so the bill can move into the new owner's name, which it can do for purchases made before November 15 of that tax year. If no bill has arrived by October 1, call 678-493-6400 or print a copy from the website. Even when the bill stays in the seller's name, the lien follows the property if it turns delinquent.

A completed PT-61 transfer form filed with the Clerk of Superior Court can replace a new real property return for the year of a sale, provided nothing was subdivided or built that year.

sections.h2: What if Cherokee County property is sold at a tax sale?
sections.html:
The buyer at a tax sale receives a tax deed, but cannot occupy, improve or evict anyone from the property right away. The owner, a creditor or anyone with an interest can redeem within 12 months.

The redemption price is the bid, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward, plus special assessments, plus a premium of 20% of the amount for the first year or part of a year and 10% for each year after that, plus sheriff and advertising costs. After 12 months the buyer may serve a notice of foreclosure of the right to redeem by certified mail to the owner of record and every interest holder, with a notice also running once a week for four consecutive weeks in the county newspaper.

If a sale brings in more than is owed, the excess funds are held and can be claimed under O.C.G.A. 48-4-5 by the record owner at the time of sale and by security deed holders. The county says nobody needs to pay or hire a third party to claim them.

faqs.q: What is the Cherokee County property tax due date?
faqs.a: November 15. Bills are mailed in September, and taxes not paid by that date are considered delinquent.

faqs.q: Does Cherokee County prorate property taxes at a sale?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner states there is no provision in the law for the office to prorate taxes for partial-year ownership, so buyer and seller must settle any split at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I file for a homestead exemption in Cherokee County?
faqs.a: File in person at the Tax Assessors' Office, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton, with a Georgia license or ID showing the property address.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem property after a tax sale?
faqs.a: You have 12 months from the sale date to redeem, after which the buyer can begin the foreclosure of the right to redeem by notice.

faqs.q: How can I find my Cherokee County tax bill if I did not receive one?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at 678-493-6400 or print a copy from cherokeecountytax.com. The office suggests doing so if a bill has not arrived by October 1.
